steps.name: Sample structure QC with the shallow library in view
caveats: A shallow library shows fewer detected genes and inflated dispersion at low counts; that appearance on the PCA is expected and is not by itself evidence of a failed or mislabelled sample
With 12 samples, PCA structure is easily driven by one sample; read PC1 against library size before attributing it to condition
steps.context: Design is 6 AD lesional vs 6 control skin biopsies, unpaired, single batch, human, gene-level Salmon counts. The persisted profile flags sample_01 as having a library size roughly 4x below the median. There is no batch column in the metadata, so batch cannot be modelled or tested.
steps.question: Do the 12 skin samples separate by condition (AD lesional vs control) on a blind VST PCA, and does sample_01 — whose library is about 4x below the median — behave like a member of its condition group or like an outlier?

grounding.reason: Two-group raw-count design with a low_depth_sample flag: blind VST + PCA(500) + distance heatmap per R-0033, and keep-inspect-report for sample_01 per R-0008 rather than default removal.

constraints: Use Python only — PyDESeq2 for the variance-stabilizing transform; do not call R
Transform is a blind VST (design-agnostic), PCA on the top 500 most variable genes
Do NOT delete sample_01 silently: keep it through QC, show it on the PCA and the distance heatmap, and report its library size and detected-gene count beside the others
Removal of any sample requires a stated reason that is not depth alone — the count model down-weights a low-depth sample through its size factor
Do not normalize, scale, or transform the counts that are handed to the downstream model; the VST here is for visualisation only
steps.description: Load /eval-eight-arms-with-python-two-group-n6-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 gene symbols x 12 sample columns) and /eval-eight-arms-with-python-two-group-n6-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows, sample id + condition). Verify column-to-row correspondence and that counts are non-negative integers. Produce: a per-sample table of total library size, number of detected genes (count > 0), and fraction of counts in the top 50 genes, with sample_01 marked; a blind variance-stabilizing transform; a PCA on the 500 most variable genes coloured by condition and labelled by sample id; a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap on the VST values; and a plot of library size against PC1 to see whether depth drives the leading axis. Write a short QC verdict naming, with a stated reason, whether sample_01 should be retained for the primary analysis. Default is retain.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample QC table is written listing library size, detected genes, and top-50-gene count fraction for all 12 samples, with sample_01's values reported explicitly beside the cohort median
A blind VST PCA on the top 500 variable genes and a VST sample-distance heatmap are saved, both labelling every sample id and colouring by condition
A stated verdict on sample_01 is written that either retains it or removes it with a reason other than library size alone
The condition labels used are the actual values in metadata.csv and the group sizes are confirmed as 6 and 6

steps.name: PyDESeq2 differential expression, lesional vs control
caveats: 6 vs 6 is a modest cohort: a gene with no significant call is not a gene with no effect, and confidence intervals on individual fold changes are wide

sample_01's low depth widens its contribution's uncertainty rather than biasing the fold change; the size factor handles the depth, so an unstable gene in the sensitivity comparison is more likely low-count noise than a real depth artefact
With no length offsets available, differential transcript usage can masquerade as differential gene expression
steps.context: Counts come from Salmon at gene level with gene symbols as the first column. No transcript-level quant.sf files and no per-gene average transcript lengths are supplied, so the tximport length-offset route is not available — the matrix must be used as given. State this in the output: without length offsets, a gene whose isoform usage shifts between conditions can be called on length rather than expression, which is a known limitation of a pre-summarised Salmon gene matrix.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between AD lesional and control skin at BH-adjusted p < 0.05, and how much does that gene list change when the shallow sample_01 is excluded?

grounding.reason: Fixed-effects two-group design with 6 replicates per group on raw counts: DESeq2 Wald + apeglm per R-0001/R-0009, minimal pre-filter per R-0002/R-0029, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering per R-0010/R-0043; R-0018's tximport length offsets cannot be honoured because only a pre-summarised gene matrix was supplied, and the step states that.

constraints: Use Python only — PyDESeq2, not R DESeq2
Pre-filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size); do not filter harder than this — independent filtering in the results step does the rest
Do not pre-normalize, scale, or log the counts before the model; median-of-ratios size factors are applied as offsets inside the negative binomial model
Set the reference level of condition explicitly to the control label as it appears in metadata.csv; do not rely on alphabetical ordering
Test is the Wald test at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on and BH adjustment; pass the same alpha 0.05 that the report uses as its cutoff
Shrink the condition coefficient with apeglm and keep the unshrunken estimate and its standard error side by side in the table

Select significant genes by padj only — never by raw p-value and never by fold change alone; if a fold-change threshold is wanted, test against it inside the model rather than filtering the estimates afterwards
Keep the count-outlier behaviour on and report the flagged genes; do not silently drop NA rows
The sensitivity fit without sample_01 is reported alongside the primary all-12 result — the primary result is the all-12 fit unless T1S1 gave a stated non-depth reason to remove
steps.description: Pre-filter to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size), then fit PyDESeq2 on the raw counts with design ~condition, control as the explicit reference level, contrast (condition, lesional, control) so a positive log2 fold change means higher in lesional. Median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the model. Run the Wald test, apply apeglm shrinkage to the condition coefficient, and extract results at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Report the number of genes tested after the pre-filter, the number with padj < 0.05, and the number with an NA p-value split by cause (count-outlier flag vs independent filter) — with 6 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance outliers and sets their p-values to NA rather than replacing counts. Save the full results table with unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and baseMean. Then repeat the entire fit on the 11 samples excluding sample_01 as a sensitivity analysis and report the overlap of the two significant gene sets and any gene whose direction flips.
acceptance_criteria: A results table for the contrast (condition, lesional, control) is written for every tested gene with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, Wald stat, pvalue, and BH padj
The reference level is control and the sign convention (positive = higher in AD lesional) is stated explicitly in the output
Counts of: genes tested after pre-filter, genes with padj < 0.05, and NA p-values separated into count-outlier-flagged vs independent-filter-removed
A histogram of unadjusted p-values is saved and its shape is described before the adjusted values are used
A sensitivity re-fit excluding sample_01 is run and the overlap with the primary significant gene set is reported as counts plus a list of direction-flipping genes

steps.name: Quasi-likelihood robustness check and high-confidence gene set
caveats: A Python quasi-likelihood implementation is not bit-identical to edgeR's; differences in dispersion estimation will produce some disagreement that is methodological rather than biological, and the report must not read every non-overlapping gene as unstable biology
Genes with low counts are where the two methods diverge most, which overlaps with the genes most affected by sample_01's depth
steps.context: At 2–11 replicates per group DESeq2 and edgeR quasi-likelihood agree on most genes but each calls some the other does not, and the disagreement grows at low counts and low replicate numbers. With one shallow library in this cohort, that disagreement is the quantity of interest. The user constraint forbids R, so the second method must be a Python implementation and the report must name which implementation was used.
steps.question: Which of the AD-lesional-vs-control genes are called by both the DESeq2 Wald test and a quasi-likelihood negative binomial test, and which are called by only one method?

grounding.reason: R-0042 asks for a two-method overlap with the intersection as the high-confidence set; R-0001 names edgeR quasi-likelihood as the second method for DESeq2, here implemented in Python because the user forbids R.

constraints: Use Python only — no R, no rpy2 bridge to edgeR
Run on the same pre-filtered gene set, the same design ~condition, and the same alpha 0.05 with BH adjustment as T1S2, so the comparison is like for like
Report the intersection as the high-confidence set; do NOT present the union of the two methods as the result
Name the second method and its package version explicitly in the output
steps.description: Refit the same contrast on the same pre-filtered count matrix and the same ~condition design using a second, independent count-based test as a robustness check — an edgeR-style quasi-likelihood negative binomial F-test implemented in Python (for example a glmGamPoi-style / statsmodels NB GLM with a quasi-likelihood F-test on the condition coefficient, using TMM or median-of-ratios offsets), applied to every gene tested in T1S2. Adjust with BH at the same alpha 0.05. Report: the number of significant genes from each method, the size of the intersection, and the two method-specific sets named by method. Treat the intersection as the high-confidence gene set and carry it forward as such. If no Python implementation of a quasi-likelihood F-test can be assembled that is faithful to the method, say so explicitly and instead report a documented alternative second test (for example a limma-voom-style weighted linear model in Python) naming exactly what was run — do not silently substitute and do not claim an edgeR result that was not produced.
acceptance_criteria: A second differential test on the identical gene set and design is run and its results table is written with per-gene statistic, p-value, and BH padj
Significant-gene counts are reported for each method separately plus the size of the intersection
The intersection is written out as the high-confidence gene set and the two method-exclusive sets are written out labelled by method
The exact second-method implementation actually used is named in the output; if a faithful quasi-likelihood F-test was not achievable in Python, that is stated plainly along with what was run instead

steps.name: Preranked hallmark GSEA on the Wald statistic
caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent: a benchmark across ten methods on 75 datasets found wide disagreement in both the number and ranking of significant sets. Present an enriched hallmark as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as a demonstrated mechanism

Count data carries a length and expression-level bias — long and highly expressed genes reach significance more easily. Using the tested genes as the universe removes the detection part of that bias but not all of it
Two hallmarks sharing most of their leading-edge genes are one finding, not two
steps.context: Gene identifiers in counts.csv are gene symbols (HGNC), and the hallmark and GO collections in the reference store are also keyed on HGNC symbols, so the ranked list and the gene sets share an identifier space directly and no Entrez conversion is needed — state the symbol-space match and the unmatched fraction rather than performing a conversion that would only add mapping loss. The hallmark collection is the resource the research question names; if it cannot be resolved at run time the step must stop and report that, because 'which hallmark pathways change' cannot be answered without it. The GO follow-up is optional enrichment: if the GO collection is absent, report its absence and proceed with hallmark alone.
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are enriched in AD lesional versus control skin, and which leading-edge genes drive each significant hallmark?

grounding.reason: Enrichment after a DE test on human data: preranked GSEA on the full tested list against MSigDB Hallmark per R-0107/R-0048; the disputed ranking metric of R-0108 is settled on the Wald statistic per R-0099. R-0098's Reactome follow-up is replaced by the GO-BP collection because the reference store holds hallmark, GO, and oncogenic human collections but no Reactome or human WikiPathways GMT.

constraints: Use Python only — gseapy prerank, not R fgsea

Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (`stat`). This is the stated choice on a disputed point: the Wald statistic is signed and scaled by its own standard error, so it does not put noisy low-count genes at the top the way an unshrunken log2 fold change does, and it does not create rank ties the way a saturated signed p-value does. State this choice in the output
Feed the FULL ranked list of tested genes — do not cut at padj or at a fold change before the test
Universe is the set of genes tested in T1S2, never the whole genome or the whole annotation
Gene set size window 15 to 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Set and record an explicit random seed for the permutations — a permutation p-value without its seed does not reproduce
Do not merge the hallmark and GO collections into one set list; run each separately with the same window and universe, and state each collection's release beside its results
Resolve the hallmark and GO collections from the environment's reference store as human (HGNC symbol) gene set collections; confirm the organism is human before use

Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list: report the size of that list, and if it is under about 50 genes state that ORA on it would be underpowered and that the ranked test on the full list is the result
steps.description: Take the full T1S2 results table — every tested gene, not a thresholded subset — and rank genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column). Run preranked GSEA (gseapy prerank) against the human MSigDB hallmark gene set collection resolved from the environment's reference store, restricting to sets with 15 to 500 members after intersection with the tested genes, with a fixed random seed and BH-adjusted permutation p-values. Report for each hallmark: normalized enrichment score, nominal p, FDR q, set size after intersection, and the leading-edge gene list with each member's Wald statistic and shrunken log2 fold change. Collapse hallmarks whose leading edges largely overlap into groups and report one representative per group, keeping the full table as a supplement. Then repeat the identical ranked test against the human GO biological process collection as a stated follow-up to resolve any hallmark hit to a more specific process, reporting each collection's release separately and never merging the two collections into one set list. Report the fraction of tested gene symbols that failed to match any set in each collection.
acceptance_criteria: Preranked GSEA is run on the full list of tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — no significance or fold-change cut is applied to the input list

A hallmark results table is written with NES, nominal p, FDR q, and post-intersection set size for every tested hallmark set, and the leading-edge genes are listed for each significant set with their per-gene statistics
The gene set size window (15–500 after intersection with tested genes), the ranking metric, the universe (tested genes), the collection name and its release version are all stated in the output
Redundant hallmarks sharing leading-edge genes are collapsed into groups with one representative reported, and the full uncollapsed table is retained
The share of tested gene symbols matching no set in each collection is reported
A GO biological process follow-up is run and reported as a separate table with its own release stated, or its absence is reported explicitly

steps.name: Integrated report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
caveats: Reporting a hallmark name without its leading edge hides which genes actually drove it, and two hallmarks with one shared leading edge is one finding
The sensitivity analysis without sample_01 is a stability check, not a second result — do not report whichever gene list is larger as the answer
steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers the research question. It must not overstate: a modest cohort with one shallow library supports a ranked hypothesis list, not a settled mechanism.
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes and which hallmark pathways change between AD lesional and control skin', and what are the limits imposed by n=6 per group and the shallow sample_01 library?

grounding.reason: Report content follows the procedure's report step: MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), shrunken plus unshrunken effect columns ranked on the shrunken value (R-0085), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat (R-0051/R-0055), leading edge per set (R-0105), and the full reproducibility record (R-0041/R-0086).

constraints: Use Python only for every figure and table
Rank genes for the tables and plots by the shrunken log2 fold change, never by the unshrunken estimate alone; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit since shrinkage does not change the test
Name the shrinkage estimator (apeglm) in the table header
State the number of significant genes from each of the two DE methods and the intersection size; do not present the union as the result
Report every enrichment parameter: collection and release, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool and version, multiple-testing method
Do not describe an enriched pathway as an established mechanism — present it as a hypothesis
Do not fabricate any number: every figure in the report must trace to an output of T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 or T2S1
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Lead with the answer: the number of differentially expressed genes at padj < 0.05, the high-confidence two-method intersection, and the significant hallmark pathways with their direction. Include the two fit diagnostics before the tables — an MA plot of shrunken log2 fold change against mean normalized count with significant genes marked, and a dispersion plot showing per-gene estimates, the fitted trend, and the shrunken values. Include the p-value histogram and describe its shape. Give the top genes ranked by shrunken log2 fold change, with the unshrunken estimate and lfcSE beside it in the table, plus a volcano plot. Report per significant hallmark its leading-edge genes and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. State the method, every package version, the design formula, the contrast and its sign convention, the thresholds, the number of genes tested, the number of DE genes, the gene set collection and its release, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the random seed, and the full session information. Devote a clearly-headed section to limitations: 6 vs 6 replicates, the retained shallow library sample_01 and how much the gene list moved when it was excluded, the absence of transcript length offsets, and the method-dependence of the enrichment result.
acceptance_criteria: The report leads with the count of DE genes at padj < 0.05, the two-method high-confidence intersection size, and the named significant hallmark pathways with direction
An MA plot and a dispersion plot appear before the gene tables, each with a stated description of what it shows, plus the p-value histogram and a volcano plot
The gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, and lfcSE per gene, with ranking done on the shrunken value
Leading-edge genes are listed per significant hallmark and the overlap between reported sets is marked
A reproducibility record is stored with the results containing session info, package versions, the permutation seed, and the gene set collection release

A limitations section explicitly names: n=6 per group, the retained sample_01 and the size of the sensitivity-analysis discrepancy, the missing transcript length offsets, and enrichment method-dependence

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, 12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples) with a 12-row metadata table giving one condition per sample: 6 atopic dermatitis lesional skin vs 6 control skin, unpaired, single batch, human. The research question is two-part — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus an explicit instruction to handle the one shallow library (sample_01, library size ~4x below the median) carefully. Every script is Python, per the user constraint; PyDESeq2 provides the DESeq2 model (median-of-ratios size factors, negative binomial Wald test, apeglm shrinkage) in Python, and gseapy provides preranked GSEA equivalent to fgsea.

The order follows the knowledge-service procedure for a two-group unpaired counts design with a low-depth flag. T1S1 does sample-structure QC first: library sizes and detected genes per sample, blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap, with sample_01 kept and explicitly placed on each plot. The knowledge rule (R-0008, R-0030) is that a depth difference alone is not grounds for removal — the size factor already down-weights the sample — so the default is retain-and-report, and any removal must carry a stated non-depth reason (e.g. sample_01 falling with the wrong condition group on PCA plus a collapsed detected-gene count). T1S2 fits the model on the primary all-12 cohort and, because the caveat is real, repeats the fit with sample_01 excluded as a sensitivity analysis so the reader sees how much of the gene list depends on that one library. T1S3 reruns the same contrast with an edgeR-style quasi-likelihood alternative implemented in Python for a robustness overlap; at n=6 per group, DESeq2 and QL agree on most genes and the intersection is the high-confidence set. T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes — every gene, not a thresholded list — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stated choice on the disputed ranking-metric rule; it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike an unshrunken fold change) and runs preranked GSEA against the MSigDB human hallmark collection, which is the resource the question names, with GO-BP as a stated follow-up. T1S4 assembles the report with the two fit diagnostics, shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes, leading-edge genes, and a reproducibility record.

Stated limits: 6 vs 6 is a modest cohort, so a null result for any given pathway is not evidence of no change; and one of the twelve libraries is shallow, which costs power specifically in that sample's group. Both belong in the report.

steps.method: VST (blind) PCA, sample distance heatmap, library size and detected gene table
Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (smallest group size)
Median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
~condition with control as explicit reference level; contrast condition lesional vs control
apeglm log fold change shrinkage (PyDESeq2 lfc_shrink)
gseapy prerank (fgsea-equivalent) on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome/WikiPathways as follow-up
Markdown report with fit diagnostics, gene table, GSEA leading edge, reproducibility record
